name: quit veto
verdict: PASS on the veto / FAIL on the documented stop contract

applescript_quit.side_finding: the daemon is still an AppleEvent-addressable application under 'prohibited' — further confirmation the LaunchServices registration persists

sigterm_1.result: VETOED. runtime.daemon.quit_request_vetoed at 02:23:45.480; process still alive after 30.022s of 50ms polling

sigterm_2.result: process died immediately (no shutdown log); launchd restarted it as pid 94460 at 02:24:33.997

defect.claim_contradicted: AGENT1-VALIDATOR/ROUND1_REVIEW.md section 3 paths 1 and 3: 'launchctl bootout -> SIGTERM. process.once(SIGTERM) sets shutdownAuthorized = true, then shutdown(0, signal:SIGTERM) -> app.exit(0)' and 'a second SIGTERM ... Node restores the default signal disposition'
defect.observed: The JS process.once('SIGTERM') handler never runs in the packaged Electron main process. Electron/Chromium's own native SIGTERM handler intercepts the signal and calls app.quit() -> before-quit -> our veto -> preventDefault(). shutdownAuthorized is never set, shutdown() is never called, and the first SIGTERM is swallowed entirely. The SECOND SIGTERM terminates the process by default disposition (consistent with a one-shot native handler), still without shutdown().
working_stop_paths: launchctl bootout -> launchd SIGKILL escalation after exit timeout = 5s
defect.wrong_operator_hint: the veto's own log line says 'use launchctl bootout/kickstart, or SIGTERM, to stop the runtime daemon' — SIGTERM does not stop it, and bootout only stops it by forced kill 5s later
defect.severity: no daemon is ever unkillable (R-1/R-2 not brickable), but every stop is a forced kill: runtimeHost.stop() never runs, so there is no graceful runtime-host shutdown on any path
